newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco's holdings pull Casablanca bourse down.
newsitem.headline: Morocco's holdings pull Casablanca bourse down.

text.p: Morocco's stock exchange closed on Tuesday 0.29 percent lower pulled down by ONA Group and Societe Nationale d'Investissement, stockbrokers said.
The Casablanca bourse all-share index closed at 635.28 points from 637.11 points on Monday.
ONA, the country's largest private holding was down six dirhams to 772 dirhams.
SNI, the second largest private group, dipped five dirhams to 715 dirhams with 1,032 shares exchanged on the market.
Banque Marocaine du Commerce Exterieur dropped 16 dirhams to 580 dirhams with 877 shares traded.
BMCE will open a representation bureau in Frankfurt on Wednesday as part of its policy to diversify its activity abroad, the spokesman said.
Maroc Leasing edged down three dirhams to 416 dirhams
First and second tranche of privatisation bonds, issued respectively in January and May 1996, were up six and 13 dirhams to respectively 1,346 and 1,175 dirhams.
Banque Commerciale du Maroc, which holds 27.5 percent of credit firm Maghrebail, rose seven dirhams to 857 dirhams with 1,017 shares traded.
Morocco said on Tuesday it would float 20 percent of Maghrebail worth 82 million dirhams ($8.7 million). Subscriptions would be open from June 30 to July 4.
Oil refinery Samir remained unchanged at 343 dirhams with 3,895 shares exchanged and 187 shares exchanged.
Steel mill Sonasid remained unchanged at 550 dirhams.
Total traded volume on the official market was 17.2 million dirhams from 14.7 million dirhams.

On the over-the-counter market, the volume was 62.9 million dirhams from 136 million dirhams the previous session. Samir accounted for main trade with 75,850 shares traded followed by 10,000 Banque Nationale pour le Developpement Economique.
